title: EMG: neuropathy
summary: Large motor unit potentials firing fast, after the loss of motor neurones.
description: The same muscle (tibialis anterior), recorded in the same way, in a man whose nerve supply to it is damaged (a radiculopathy: an injured nerve root, L5). Fewer motor units are left, so each has to fire faster; and the surviving motor neurones have taken over muscle fibres that lost their nerve, so their potentials are large. Compare it with the healthy muscle: all three EMG recordings open on the same scale (−3.5 to +3.5 mV) and the same time scale.
look_for: The size of the motor unit potentials, compared with the healthy muscle
The rate at which one motor unit fires: measure the interval between its potentials

channels.name: EMG (tibialis anterior)
channels.about: a concentric needle electrode in the muscle; all three EMG recordings open on this scale, −3.5 to +3.5 mV

subject.notes: Chronic low back pain and a neuropathy from a right L5 radiculopathy, as the database records.
